title: Proxy delimiter undetected causing function output boundary misalignments in VPC routed requests
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers using VPC/private deployments reported intermittent failures where function/tool-calling payloads arriving from the model stream were mis-framed, causing downstream structured-output parsers to drop or concatenate function call boundaries. Affected environments: Private (VPC) and Dedicated routed through customer-managed proxies; some Hosted paths that traverse our edge proxy when proxy rewriting is enabled.

Symptoms observed:
- Customer-visible symptoms: truncated JSON payloads inside function invocation objects, interleaved key/values, or duplicate function call entries in a single response.
- Platform signals: spike in 'structured_parser_error' logs, increase in user-reported JSON.parse exceptions, and elevated error rate for function-invoke routes (chat.invoke_tool).
- Occurs under network paths that perform HTTP body re-encoding or proxy layer chunk-reassembly (customer proxies, private edge, and some dedicated NAT configurations).

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Use the attached repro harness (repro.sh) to run a chat -> model streaming request that triggers function invocation with large nested JSON result (~4–8KB).
2) Route traffic through a Toxiproxy-like middlebox configured to re-chunk and add a Content-Encoding header (gzip offload simulation).
3) Observe parser errors in the runtime logs and verify that function call separators (0x1E framing) are either dropped or shifted into adjacent chunk boundaries, producing invalid concatenated JSON.

Initial triage and findings:
- Root cause: Our streaming framing relies on an ASCII record separator (0x1E) delimiter being preserved by the proxy chain. Certain proxy/rewrite combinations (notably proxies that re-chunk streamed bodies or perform streaming decompression/recompression) can either strip or coalesce chunk boundaries, which causes the runtime's incremental JSON detector to miss the intended frame break and treat two adjacent framed JSON objects as a single blob.
- Contributing factors: a) some of our proxy code paths were performing a naive UTF-8 normalization step that silently removed an ASCII control char when reconstructing chunks; b) the parser's streaming boundary heuristics only looked for newline and bracket transitions and did not robustly fall back to delimiter-aware framing for corrupted streams.
- Scope: Reports from three customers in the last 48 hours (SUP-14092, SUP-14107, SUP-14109). Repro in lab with deterministic proxy config.

Customer impact: high — customers experienced incorrect function routing, missing tool calls, and user-visible failures inside production flows (ticketed escalations and page incidents).

Temporary mitigation (already applied):
- Hotfix 1: Edge proxy config updated to preserve 0x1E bytes during re-chunking and to disable the UTF-8 normalization rewrite for VPC-proxied streaming requests. Deployed to private control plane and Dedicated edge immediately (rollback-safe).
- Hotfix 2: Runtime fallback: added a quick-path in the streaming parser to attempt re-synchronizing on valid JSON object boundaries when delimiter missing and emit a detailed debug event. This reduces customer-visible failures but is not a full fix.

Proposed permanent fix (details in PR):
- Make the streaming protocol explicit: include a short per-message framing header (4-byte length prefix + 1 byte 'frame type') at the transport layer for all inter-service streaming between edge/proxy -> runtime to avoid reliance on non-printable delimiter bytes.
- Update streaming parser to be tolerant: implement a boundary-resync algorithm that can handle delimiter loss by scanning for top-level JSON object boundaries and using size hints when available.
- Add integration tests that simulate re-chunking, decompression/recompression, and proxy rewriting to ensure delimiters are preserved or that the resync algorithm recovers.

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR to runtime branch and cut runtime-1.20.1-hotfix for Dedicated and Private control plane; apply to Hosted edge as canary 5% traffic for 48 hours.
- Stepwise ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours if telemetry shows parser-error rate < baseline.
- Backout: revert hotfix branch, restore proxy normalization setting if regression observed.

Monitoring and success criteria:
- Primary metrics: structured_parser_error rate, function_invoke_error rate, SUP-14092/14107/14109 ticket counts.
- Target: reduce parser_error rate to pre-incident baseline within 24h of full rollout.

Follow-ups and engineering notes:
- Add explicit end-to-end integration tests in CI that exercise private-proxy and dedicated-proxy network behaviors.
- Add customer-facing runbook for support to collect streaming raw payloads and provide reproductible proxy configs.
- Consider long-term migration away from single-byte delimiters for any public protocol surface.

2026-03-03 Priya Nair: Implemented parser quick-fallback for resync; staged unit tests. Push PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9721 for early review.

2026-03-09 Security review (Rashid Malik): reviewed network framing change proposal. No direct secrets exposure; requested additional threat modeling for replay/length-prefix abuse before GA. Marking for follow-up.
2026-03-11 Priya Nair: Addressed code review comments, added integration tests for VPC re-chunking; preparing canary deployment manifest. Need ops approval for private control plane patch window.

current_workaround: Edge proxy normalization setting disabled for affected customer routes and runtime quick-fallback parsing enabled to reduce visible failures; recommend customers strip custom re-chunk rules or upgrade proxy to preserve ASCII control chars until runtime patch is applied.
